intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is caused by biallelic mutation in the RAB34 gene (610917) on chromosome 17q11.2.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is caused by biallelic mutation in the RAB34 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34 in four individuals from three unrelated families. Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34)
checks.explanation: The abstract links bi-allelic RAB34 variants to a new form of OFDS. The OFD20 label is standard nomenclature for that disorder.

checks.claim: The RAB34 gene is located on chromosome 17q11.2.
checks.evidence_quote: compound heterozygous variants in the RAB34 gene
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene the paper names. The abstract itself does not give 17q11.2.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is an autosomal recessive form of oral-facial-digital syndrome caused by biallelic RAB34 mutations. Bruel et al. (2023) described the disorder as OFDS-RAB34. Besides oral-facial-digital features, it includes cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.

checks.evidence_quote: We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34 in four individuals from three unrelated families.
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic variants point to recessive inheritance, but the abstract never says 'autosomal recessive'.

checks.explanation: The abstract reports bi-allelic RAB34 variants as the cause of the disorder.

paragraphs.text: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) reported a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype and multiple malformations. These were posterior neck edema, micrognathia, low-set and small ears, auricular hypoplasia, cleft lip and palate, and short extremities. The fetus also had both preaxial and postaxial polydactyly, a combination that rarely occurs.

paragraphs.text: Bruel et al. (2023) found biallelic RAB34 mutations in affected individuals from 3 unrelated families. Batkovskyte et al. (2024) found compound heterozygous RAB34 mutations in an affected fetus, with 1 mutation inherited from each parent. These findings indicate that OFD20 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

paragraphs.text: Bruel et al. (2023) used exome sequencing to study 4 individuals with oral-facial-digital syndrome from 3 unrelated families. In all of them, they identified biallelic missense mutations in the RAB34 gene. The mutations clustered near the C terminus of RAB34. In functional studies, the mutant RAB34 proteins showed strong loss of function. Some mutants could still be recruited to the mother centriole, but cells expressing mutant RAB34 had a significant defect in cilium assembly.

paragraphs.text: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) used genome sequencing to study a fetus with a skeletal ciliopathy phenotype. They identified compound heterozygous mutations in the RAB34 gene. One was a maternally inherited missense mutation, c.254T-C, causing an ile85-to-thr (I85T) substitution. The other was a paternally inherited nonsense mutation, c.691C-T, causing an arg231-to-ter (R231X) substitution. An unaffected sib carried only the paternal mutation. The authors noted that Rab34-null mice display a ciliopathy phenotype with cleft palate and polydactyly, which supported pathogenicity.

paragraphs.text: Bruel et al. (2023) found that mutant RAB34 proteins showed strong loss of function. Cells expressing mutant RAB34 had a significant defect in cilium assembly, even though some mutants could still be recruited to the mother centriole. RAB34 acts selectively in cell types that use the intracellular ciliogenesis pathway. The authors concluded that RAB34 is the first small GTPase involved in OFDS.
